items.statement: Total copper metal sales fell 16% and Continuous Cast Rod sales declined 8% compared to the prior-year quarter.
items.quote: Copper metal sales at 105 KT, down 16% Copper Continuous Cast Rod (CCR) sales at 96 KT, down 8%

items.statement: Hindalco's consolidated net debt to EBITDA rose to 1.95x as of June 30, 2026, up from 1.02x a year earlier.
items.quote: Consolidated Net Debt to EBITDA at 1.95x as of June 30, 2026 vs 1.02x a year ago

items.statement: Management is maintaining an active pipeline of strategic investments across both upstream capacities and downstream value-added projects.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our pipeline of strategic investments remains robust across upstream and downstream. As we continue to expand upstream capacities in alumina, aluminium and copper, we are scaling up our downstream projects.

items.statement: Commercial shipments from the Bay Minette plant are projected to begin in Q1 FY28.
items.quote: Bay Minette plant commissioning is underway; expect to commence commercial shipments in Q1 FY28

items.statement: Aditya Smelter Phase 2 is targeted to commence metal production in FY28.
items.quote: Aditya Smelter Phase 2 on track to begin metal production in FY28

items.statement: Total domestic aluminium demand in India is estimated to reach 1,491 Kt in Q1 FY27, representing 3% year-on-year growth led by the automotive segment.
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, the total Indian demand is likely to reach 1,491 Kt, up 3% YoY, primarily led by strong demand in Auto segment

items.statement: Novelis' quarterly revenue expanded by 23% to $5.8 billion primarily because of higher prevailing metal prices.
items.quote: Revenue at $5.8 billion, up 23%, driven by higher metal prices

items.statement: Novelis' EBITDA rose 37% aided by the restart of the Oswego hot mill and accelerating cost optimisation measures.
items.quote: Novelis recorded a 37% improvement in EBITDA, buoyed by the successful restart of Oswego hot mill and accelerated benefits from its cost optimisation programme.

items.statement: Aluminium Upstream EBITDA margins rose to 55% from 44% in Q1 FY26 on the back of favorable macro conditions.
items.quote: EBITDA (₹ Crore) ↑ 81% at all-time high backed by favourable macros leading to margins increase to 55% vs. 44% in Q1 FY26

items.statement: Hindalco commissioned the battery foil unit at Aditya and coated AC fins plant at Taloja while ramping up its Aditya FRP facility.
items.quote: Aluminium Battery foil plant at Aditya and Coated AC Fins plant at Taloja commissioned; FRP plant at Aditya scaling up to optimal production levels

items.statement: Hindalco operationalised a 65 MW captive round-the-clock renewable energy project at Aditya Aluminium.
items.quote: Operationalised a 65 MW round-the-clock renewable energy project at Aditya Aluminium, making Hindalco the only company in India with an operational captive round-the-clock renewable energy plant

items.statement: A severe supply shock is pushing up LME aluminium prices and is expected to widen the global CY26 market deficit to roughly 1.0 million tonnes.
items.quote: Largest ever supply shock driving up LME. Despite demand weakness, global deficit is likely to widen to ~1.0 mt in CY26 (pre-conflict: deficit of 0.3 million)

items.statement: positive
items.quote: Together, these investments position Hindalco uniquely as an integrated global metals company with the right balance of upstream strength and downstream value addition to deliver sustainable, long-term growth.

items.statement: Consolidated segment EBITDA grew 58% year-on-year to INR 13,481 crores, and consolidated profit after tax increased 75% to INR 7,013 crores.
items.quote: Our consolidated business segment EBITDA was up 58% year-on-year at INR13,481 crores this quarter. The consolidated profit after tax was up 75% on a year-on-year basis at INR7,013 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Quarterly copper EBITDA rose 36% year-on-year to a record INR 918 crores due to improved byproduct realizations and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: Our quarterly copper EBITDA stood at a record INR918 crores, up 36% year-on-year. on account of better realizations in byproducts and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Refined copper demand in India declined 9% year-on-year to 359 Kt during the quarter.
items.quote: Total demand, including domestic supplies and scrap in quarter 1 of FY27, stood at 359 Kt compared to 396 Kt in the same period last year, reflecting a 9% year-on-year decline.

items.statement: Indian copper business metal shipments fell 16% year-on-year to 105 Kt because of a scheduled maintenance shutdown.
items.quote: On India's copper business performance this quarter, our overall metal shipments were at 105 Kt, down 16% year-on-year due to the planned maintenance shutdown.

items.statement: Novelis shipments dropped 5% year-on-year to 916 KT from 963 KT in the prior-year period.
items.quote: Novelis recorded shipments of 916 KT, reflecting a decline of 5% year-on-year over 963 KT shipments in the same period last year.

items.statement: Management expects the global aluminum market to register a 1 million ton deficit in calendar year 2026.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain constructive on aluminum. The market is expected to have a deficit of 1 million tons in calendar year '26 compared to pre-conflict expectations of about 0.3 million tons.

items.statement: Novelis reaffirmed its long-term guidance of $600 EBITDA per ton, supported by structural cost-reduction programs.
items.quote: Importantly, our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged. This confidence is supported by the accelerated execution of our $350 million to $400 million structural cost reduction programs

items.statement: Management anticipates higher sequential volumes in Q2 for both copper and downstream aluminum.
items.quote: I think the volumes in Q2, both for copper and downstream aluminum will be higher. I mean, as I said in my prepared remarks, the electrical sector was a little bit weak.

items.statement: Annual brand royalty payments are capped at INR 225 crores.
items.quote: Yes. And it's capped at INR225 crores. And I think it's important to note for us this royalty amount is below what we say is our materiality threshhold.

items.statement: Management expects captive coal output of about 1 million tons from Chakla and 0.5 million tons from Bandha in FY28.
items.quote: Chakla back to commence, we are expecting about 1 million tons from Chakla, Bandha will only start from the middle of the year. So I would say about 0.5 million tons for Bandha.

items.statement: Management expects costs to increase by 5% to 6% in Q2 FY27 compared to Q1 FY27 in rupee terms.
items.quote: Our costs went up by about 5% Q1 to Q4, and we are expecting another 5%, 6% Q2 to Q1 in rupee terms.

items.statement: Indian aluminum demand grew roughly 3% year-on-year to about 1.5 million tons in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We estimate aluminum demand in quarter 1 of FY27 at around 1.5 million tons representing growth of approximately 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Indian refined copper demand softened due to customer inventory adjustments and cautious purchasing amid regional geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: In India, refined copper demand remained somewhat subdued during the quarter, driven by inventory optimization by customers and a more cautious purchasing approach amid uncertainties arising from the West India conflict.

items.statement: Domestic demand for flat rolled products expanded by more than 10% year-on-year, led by packaging and consumer durables.
items.quote: Within domestic products, flat rolled products performed particularly well with demand growing by more than 10% year-on-year, driven primarily by strong demand from packaging and consumer durable.

items.statement: Copper concentrate treatment and refining charges remained historically low and reached negative ranges between minus 26 cents and minus 30 cents per pound.
items.quote: Availability of concentrate was tight across the industry and treatments and refining charges stayed at historically low levels at times even negative levels at the range of minus 26 cents to minus 30 cents per pound.

items.statement: Higher metal premiums supported downstream margins, with USD 250 per ton regarded as a sustainable normalized level.
items.quote: So high MJP has helped us get those margins on the downstream also up. So I would say more around USD250 is a more sustainable number.

items.statement: Novelis achieved run-rate cost savings of $225 million as it accelerated cost efficiency initiatives.
items.quote: With another quarter of solid execution behind us, that run rate cost savings are now at $225 million as we accelerate all cost efficiency initiatives.

items.statement: Hindalco anticipates rising coal prices in the northern region during the monsoon period after utilizing lower-cost inventory in Q1.
items.quote: And Indrajit, I think actually, we benefited from some of the low-cost inventories during quarter one. And quarter two, the coal prices in the northern region have gone up in the monsoon period.

items.statement: Indian upstream aluminum generated a record EBITDA of USD 2,331 per ton with a record EBITDA margin of 55%.
items.quote: This delivered an all-time high EBITDA of USD2,331 per ton this quarter. EBITDA margins were at a record 55% and continue to be amongst the best in the global industry.

items.statement: Quarterly EBITDA for Indian downstream aluminum rose 30% year-on-year to INR 298 crores.
items.quote: Aluminum downstream delivered a quarterly EBITDA of INR298 crores, up by 30% year-on-year this quarter versus INR229 crores in the prior period.

items.statement: Hindalco expects its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to remain fairly stable over coming quarters because this is a high capital expenditure year in India.
items.quote: Yes. I think on the India side, Pinakin, this is a high capex year for us. So I don't expect our net debt-to-EBITDA to materially change across the coming quarters.

items.statement: Management noted that FY28 will be a high capital expenditure year and aims to protect cash flows via commodity hedging.
items.quote: Our view on FY28 is that once the Middle East smelters come back, we think that 3,200 is a good level for FY28. It's a high capex year for us, so we want to protect our cash flows

items.statement: The 600 KT Bay Minette rolling and recycling facility is on track to complete construction this year.
items.quote: The 600 KT Bay Minette greenfield rolling and recycling facility, which is on track for completion this year represents a transformational milestone for Novelis.

items.statement: The Aditya smelter expansion will occur in two 180-pot phases, commissioning in December 2027 and December 2028.
items.quote: The expansion is in 2 phases, 180-180. The first 180 will come in December of '27. The next 180 will come in December of '28 we will still be net long of alumina

items.statement: Consolidated net debt to EBITDA stood at 1.95x as of June 2026, below the company's threshold of 2x.
items.quote: As of June 2026, our consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA stood at 1.95x below our stated threshold of 2x.

items.statement: Novelis management confirmed visibility that leverage will decline below 4x.
items.quote: Yes. So, I already said that based on all the visibility that I can see right now, we will be below 4x.

items.statement: Hindalco reached 470 megawatts of renewable capacity and 35 megawatts of pumped storage tie-ups under its round-the-clock program.
items.quote: As of the end of Q1, we have 470 megawatts of renewable energy capacity across solar, wind, hydro resources along with 35 megawatts of pump storage tie-ups under our round-the-clock renewable energy program.

items.statement: Hindalco is advancing copper smelter expansion, e-waste recycling, and an Inner Grooved Tubes project to strengthen downstream and value-added capabilities.
items.quote: Our copper smelter expansion, e-waste recycling projects and other sustainability-led initiatives are progressing as planned. In addition, the Inner Grooved Tubes project will further strengthen our downstream portfolio and enhance our value-added product capabilities.

items.statement: Chinese aluminum production grew roughly 3% year-on-year to nearly 11 million tons in the first quarter of calendar year 2026.
items.quote: Looking at the global aluminum market in quarter 1 of calendar year '26 Chinese aluminum production grew about 3% year-on-year to nearly 11 million tons supported by capacity additions in regions such as Yunnan

items.statement: Global copper production rose 2.6% year-on-year to 7.2 million tons in Q2 CY26, resulting in a global deficit of around 0.3 million tons against demand of 7.5 million tons.
items.quote: In quarter 2 of calendar year '26, the global copper production grew 2.6% year-on-year to 7.2 million tons, while consumption increased more modestly to 7.5 million tons, resulting in a net global deficit

items.statement: Domestic economic growth faces downside risks from geopolitical uncertainties, international market volatility, external headwinds, and weather disruptions.
items.quote: However, downside risk persists particularly from geopolitical uncertainties, volatility in global financial markets, external headwinds and weather-related disruptions.

items.statement: positive
items.quote: And I think the significant part for us was the strength of Novelis' performance in Q1, which I think is going to get better as we go forward this year. So overall, I think that Hindalco is poised for a good FY27.
